subject: SIG: Clarify Redwood hosting options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) for Zenora review
messages:

Subject: SIG follow-up — we need a concise explanation of deployment options

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking our SIG. One of our reviewers asked for a short, vendor-friendly summary that explains the differences between Redwood's Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment modes — specifically around: data residency, who controls keys, network isolation, and operational responsibility for incident response.

Could you provide a one-page explanation we can attach to the SIG response? We're on a bit of a schedule for our compliance committee next week. If possible please also call out where to find audit evidence (SOC 2 reports, audit logs) for each mode.

Appreciate it — a short table or bullets will be perfect.

Best,
Lydia
Security Operations
Zenora Health


From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — we need a concise explanation of deployment options

Hi Lydia —

Thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise, shareable summary you can attach to the SIG response. I also attached a one-page matrix that maps the four criteria you requested to each mode, plus pointers to where evidence lives.

Executive summary (short):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Fully managed inference served from Redwood's hosted control plane. Best for quick time-to-value; Redwood controls keys, storage, and runtime. Data transit and at-rest encryption enabled by default; customers can request SOC 2 artifacts and per-tenant audit logs. Suitable when customers are comfortable with vendor-managed keys and multi-tenant runtime isolation.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Dedicated GPU pools in Redwood-managed infrastructure. Stronger logical isolation and predictable performance; Redwood still manages the control plane and keys by default but we offer customer KMS integrations in many contracts (bring-your-own-key for encryption at rest). Customers get per-deployment audit logs and an SLA. Good for regulated workloads that need capacity guarantees but still allow Redwood to operate the underlying platform.

- Private (VPC / On-prem): Customer-managed networking and optionally customer-hosted control plane. Full data residency options and customer-controlled key management (KMS/HSM). Redwood provides the runtime package and operational runbooks; responsibilities for network ACLs, host-level hardening, and physical security fall to the customer when on-prem. Evidence (e.g., SOC2 report references, deployment manifests, and audit log export formats) are provided, but some artifacts (host-level configs) will be customer-specific.

Quick mapping (for SIG answers):
- Data residency: Hosted — vendor-region; Dedicated — can be region-restricted; Private — customer-controlled (VPC or on-prem).
- Key control: Hosted — Redwood-managed keys; Dedicated — Redwood-managed or BYOK; Private — customer-managed KMS/HSM.
- Network isolation: Hosted — multi-tenant with logical isolation; Dedicated — single-tenant pools with network segmentation; Private — full VPC or on-prem isolation under customer control.
- Incidents & ops: Hosted — Redwood handles detection/response and notifies customers; Dedicated — Redwood handles infra ops, coordinated runbook with customer; Private — shared model (Redwood supports runtime but customer handles network/host ops if on-prem).

Where to find evidence: 
- SOC 2 report: available on request (link provided in our NDA portal).
- Audit logs: Per-tenant export available (Hosted/Dedicated); for Private we provide the export schema and the mechanisms to ship logs to customer's SIEM.
- Configuration manifests and deployment diagrams: Delivered as part of Private onboarding or Dedicated committed-capacity packets.

Next steps / ask:
1) I attached a PDF matrix (redwood-deployment-matrix.pdf) you can attach to the SIG.
2) If the committee needs a BYOK commitment or example KMS integration for Dedicated, we can include a short addendum.
3) Let me know if you want a one-paragraph version tailored for procurement (I can send that separately).

Attachments: redwood-deployment-matrix.pdf (one-page matrix)

Regards,
Evelyn Hart

Thanks — attaching two artifacts for your SIG bundle: 1) redwood-deployment-matrix.pdf (one-page compare table); 2) sig-evidence-checklist.xlsx (detailed list of artifacts we can provide and items the customer must supply in Private deployments).

Summary (2 lines to paste into the SIG):
Redwood supports three serving modes: Hosted (fastest onboarding, vendor-managed keys and runtime), Dedicated (single-tenant GPU pools with optional BYOK and dedicated audit logs), and Private (VPC or on-prem deployments where the customer controls network and keys). Evidence for SOC 2 and exportable audit logs are available for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private deployments we deliver configuration manifests and the audit export schema while customers retain host-level responsibility.

Next steps: Please confirm if your committee prefers a BYOK commitment for Dedicated or a deeper example of the KMS integration — we can produce a short technical addendum.

Attachments: redwood-deployment-matrix.pdf; sig-evidence-checklist.xlsx; encryption-keyflow-diagram.png
